notes: Bundler-plugin route: bugseeRollupPlugin from @bugsee/bundler-plugin-core injects debug ids and uploads source maps at build time. Source maps must be enabled (output.sourcemap); the wizard only reports that switch, it never edits it. The plugin reads the app token from BUGSEE_APP_TOKEN. From SDK 0.1.0-beta.7 the plugin also reads the token from .env.bugsee-build-plugin (the file the wizard writes); older SDKs need BUGSEE_APP_TOKEN exported. In CI, export BUGSEE_APP_TOKEN. The plugin does nothing without an app token. By default it deletes the .map files from the build output after a fully successful upload (deleteMaps: false keeps them), so they are not deployed. A build that pins script hashes with Subresource Integrity in its emitted HTML is warned about or refused. Hashes pinned elsewhere, such as in a server-side manifest or a page rendered at request time, are not detected and can break scripts silently: check those builds for integrity pins before enabling the plugin. pnpm 11 approvals: the install script of the plugin's CLI dependency must be approved, and its name depends on the SDK (@bugsee/cli from 0.1.0-beta.7, @bugsee/bugsee-cli before), so both are written to allowBuilds; the one the project does not use is a harmless pre-approval and is removed again by uninstall.
verify: Verify symbolication in a production build: serve or deploy it (not the dev server), trigger a test error from it (for example a button that throws new Error('Bugsee test error')), then open the report in the Bugsee dashboard. The stack should show your original files, functions and lines; minified positions such as a.js:1:48210 mean the source maps were not uploaded for this build or do not match it.
